original_question: For integers p, q, k with p >= q >= k + 1, Matousek's theorem states that there is a constant c(p,q,k) such that every k-uniform hypergraph satisfying the (p,q)-property has transversal number at most c(p,q,k). Is it possible to choose this bound with asymptotic growth c(p,q,k) = O(p^k)?
target_in_paper: No matching statement exists in arXiv:0902.4207. The cited paper is about quadratic stochastic operators and their open problems, not hypergraph transversal numbers, the (p,q)-property, or Matousek-style piercing bounds.

The intended direction—improving the growth of a bound c(p,q,k)—is also clear.

refined_question: For fixed integers k>=1 and q>=k+1, does there exist a constant C=C(k,q) such that for every integer p>=q and every finite k-uniform hypergraph H with the property that among every p edges of H some q have a common vertex, the transversal number tau(H) satisfies tau(H) <= C p^k?
justification: I inspected arXiv:0902.4207 itself. Its title is "Quadratic Stochastic Operators: Results and Open Problems," and the abstract states that the paper surveys results and open problems about quadratic stochastic operators. Section 1 introduces QSOs as population-evolution operators, Section 2 gives definitions, and subsequent sections list open problems about Volterra, permuted Volterra, k-Volterra, strictly non-Volterra, bistochastic, and surjective QSOs. Nothing in the paper concerns hypergraphs, the (p,q)-property, transversal numbers, or Matousek's theorem. Therefore the draft cannot be aligned faithfully with the supplied paper; the best possible response is to (i) flag the source mismatch and (ii) sharpen the draft into a self-contained research question independently of the cited paper.
